privacy.heading: Privacy
privacy.subheading: What this site collects, why, and who else sees it.

who.title: Who runs this site
who.body: Mohammad M. Khani, based in Athens, Greece, runs this site and is responsible for the data described here. For anything about your data, email <link>{email}</link>.

browsing.title: Just browsing
browsing.body: No ads, no third-party analytics and no tracking cookies. Fonts are served from this site, not from a third party. Skill pages count visits on this server only (see “If you buy a skill”).
browsing.cloudflare: Every request passes through Cloudflare, which sits in front of the server as a proxy and CDN. Cloudflare processes your IP address to deliver the page.

device.title: What is stored in your browser
device.theme: Your light or dark theme choice, in local storage.
device.intro: A flag in session storage, so the home page's intro animation plays once per visit.
device.locale: A cookie that remembers your language. It is set only when that differs from your browser's language, and cleared when you close the browser.
device.note: None of these identify you. The only login cookie on the site belongs to the owner's admin area and is never set for visitors.

contact.title: If you send a message
contact.body: The contact form stores your name, email address, message and IP address in a database on this site's own server. The IP address is used to limit each address to five messages a day. Your name, email and message are also emailed to Mohammad through Resend, an email delivery service, so Mohammad can reply.

booking.title: If you book a call
booking.stored: The booking form stores your name, email address, the time you chose, your topic and notes if you add them, your language and time zone, and your IP address in the same database. The IP address and email are used to limit bookings per day.
booking.calendar: It then creates an event with a Google Meet link on Mohammad's Google Calendar and adds you as a guest. Google receives your name, email, topic and notes, and sends you the invitation.
booking.email: A confirmation with a calendar file is emailed to you through Resend, and Mohammad is emailed your name, email, chosen time, topic and notes. Cancelling with the link in that email deletes the calendar event and marks the booking as cancelled.

shop.title: If you buy a skill
shop.stored: Starting a purchase stores an order in the same database: the product, the network and token you picked, the amount, the receiving address, the time and your IP address. The IP address limits orders and payment checks per day. When you paste a transaction hash it is stored with the order, together with a scrambled (hashed) copy of your download link.
shop.visits: Opening a skill page counts one visit in the same database: a scrambled (hashed) visitor code made from your IP address that changes every day (the IP address itself is not stored for a visit), the name of the site that sent you, like instagram.com, the page language and the time. A tap on the WhatsApp button is counted the same way. Mohammad gets an email through Resend when someone opens the page, taps WhatsApp or starts an order, with these counts and nothing that names you.
shop.chain: To check the payment, the server looks the transaction up on a public Ethereum node (PublicNode) or Tron node (TronGrid). The transfer itself, including the wallet you paid from, is public on the blockchain anyway. Mohammad is emailed the order and the transaction hash through Resend.
shop.whatsapp: If you message on WhatsApp instead, WhatsApp handles that conversation under its own terms.

retention.title: How long it is kept
retention.body: Messages and bookings are kept until they are no longer needed, and deleted when you ask. Nothing is deleted automatically.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.body: Under the GDPR you can ask to see the data held about you, have it corrected or deleted, or object to its use. Email <link>{email}</link>. If you think your data has been mishandled, you can complain to the Hellenic Data Protection Authority.

trailReel.sub: Your trip as a 3D map video, from one sentence. A Claude Code skill: tell Claude where you went, or give it a GPX file, and it renders a 1080 x 1920 route video for reels on your own computer. A globe for flights, real mountains for road trips, a city's real buildings for walks.

runs.heading: Three real runs
runs.sub: Each video was one sentence, typed into a clean Claude Code with only Trail Reel installed. The skill picks the world from the trip. The numbers below are from those runs.

world.title: Globe, for flights
world.body: A relief globe. Each flight's arc lifts off and lands, and a small plane rides the line.
world.prompt: “Make a map video of my trip: I flew from Lisbon to Dubai and then on to Bali, in the ink look.”

dolomites.title: Mountains, for road trips, rides and hikes
dolomites.body: Real elevation. The route runs on the real roads over the passes.
dolomites.prompt: “Make a map video of my Dolomites road trip from Ortisei over Passo Sella, Passo Pordoi and Passo Giau to Cortina d'Ampezzo, in the ink look.”
dolomites.extra: It also corrected Cortina's map pin to the town centre by itself.

rome.title: City, for walks
rome.body: The city's real buildings. The route runs on the real streets.
rome.prompt: “Make a map video of my walk in Rome from the Colosseum to the Pantheon, the Trevi Fountain and the Spanish Steps, in the ink look.”

runs.why: Travel map apps charge a subscription (TravelAnimator Pro is {price} a month on its own site), and free exports carry the app's watermark. Trail Reel is one payment. It runs on your computer: no app, no watermark, no credits per video.

say.title: You describe the trip
say.body: One sentence with the places, in order. Or give it a GPX file. Ask for the atlas or the ink look.

world.title: It picks the world
world.body: A flight gets the relief globe. A road trip, ride or hike gets real mountains. A walk gets the city's real buildings.

route.title: It finds the route
route.body: It downloads the open map data once: elevation tiles and OpenStreetMap roads and buildings. Then it finds the way on the real roads like a sat nav does, with its own shortest-path search. No routing server, no API keys, no account.

render.title: It renders the video
render.body: A 1080 x 1920 video for reels, made on your own computer. Pins drop on every stop, names appear and a counter shows the real distance.
